title: Olympus Mons vs Everest
subtitle: The tallest volcano
yt_title: Olympus Mons vs Mount Everest 🌋 | Ep. 96 #shorts
description:
Episode 96 of a daily journey through the universe. 🌋
We climb Olympus Mons on Mars: about 22 km high, almost three times Everest's 8,849 m, about 600 km wide, slopes so gentle you would barely notice climbing, cliffs kilometers tall, and why Mars can grow volcanoes this big.

➡️ Tomorrow, Episode 97: Next stop, Valles Marineris. A canyon as long as the United States is wide.
Start from Episode 1 "Leaving Earth" on the channel.
Follow so you don't miss a stop. A new episode every day.

#space #olympusmons #astronomy #shorts #science

segments.text: Episode ninety-six. Next stop... Olympus Mons versus Mount Everest.
Mount Everest is the tallest mountain on Earth. Eight thousand eight hundred and forty-nine meters above sea level.
Now meet Olympus Mons, on Mars. It rises about twenty-two kilometers. Almost three times taller than Everest.
It's one of the tallest mountains in the solar system, a giant volcano.
segments.headline: A giant volcano

segments.text: And it's wide. About six hundred kilometers across, roughly the size of Arizona.
segments.headline: As wide as Arizona

segments.text: Its slopes are so gentle that if you climbed it, you'd barely notice you were going up. And from the top, the base would be hidden beyond the horizon.
segments.headline: You wouldn't notice the climb

segments.text: At its edges, cliffs drop kilometers straight down.
segments.headline: Giant cliffs

segments.text: Why so big? Mars has weaker gravity, and no moving plates. Lava kept erupting in the same spot for millions of years.
segments.headline: Lava in one place

segments.text: On Earth, the plates keep sliding, so volcanoes like Hawaii's form chains instead of one giant.
segments.headline: Earth's version

segments.text: But right next door, Mars has a scar so long it would stretch across the United States. Follow, so you don't miss episode ninety-seven.
